quiz_title: 🧠 AI Challenge 4: Voice Mazes & Smart Home Text NLP

questions.question: What type of machine learning training lets a computer classify spoken words or audio commands?
questions.explanation: Correct! An Audio Classifier trains on acoustic frequencies to recognize spoken words or sound profiles.

questions.question: How do you collect data samples to train a custom Audio Classifier model?
options: By recording multiple short sound clips or voice recordings of the target commands (like 'Up', 'Down')
questions.explanation: Excellent! Recording vocal repetitions compiles audio waveforms used to train acoustic nodes.

questions.question: Which game component is excellent to steer using vocal audio commands?
options: A sprite inside a maze corridor (moving up, down on voice triggers)
questions.explanation: Perfect! Voice commands are perfect to steer maze sprites without keyboard arrows.

questions.question: What block trigger runs immediately when the Audio Classifier hears the specific word 'Right'?
questions.explanation: Spot on! The 'when heard (word)' block is an event listener that fires code when matching vocals are sensed.

questions.question: What does NLP stand for in advanced artificial intelligence?
options: Natural Language Processing (teaching computers to understand written text sentences)
questions.explanation: Great! Natural Language Processing involves teaching computers to read, parse, and extract meaning from text statements.

questions.question: What is Text Classification in machine learning?
options: Training a model to identify the underlying intent or meaning of a typed sentence
questions.explanation: Perfect! Text classification maps natural sentences to specific logic categories (intents).

questions.question: If a user types 'Turn on the lights' or 'It is dark here', what intent should a smart home NLP model classify these as?
questions.explanation: Spot on! Both sentences share the same fundamental intent: activating the light source ('turn_on').

questions.question: Which block returns the classified intent string of a natural sentence input?
questions.explanation: Great! The 'get classified intent' block parses text inputs and returns matching trained tags.

questions.question: How can you feed typed text inputs from a player into your NLP model?
options: Using the 'ask () and wait' sensor block, then passing the 'answer' block into the text classifier
questions.explanation: Excellent! Snapping the sensor's 'answer' block feeds typed inputs directly into the NLP text analyzer.

questions.question: In a Voice Maze game, if the sprite hears 'Left', what block sequence should run to slide it left?
questions.explanation: Perfect! Sliding horizontally left requires reducing the X coordinate value by a negative speed offset.

questions.question: Coding Task: Write block pseudo-code to make a sprite change X by 15 when the Audio Classifier hears the command 'Go'.
questions.explanation: Outstanding! Snapping coordinate adjustments to audio listeners automates voice navigation!

questions.question: Coding Task: Write block pseudo-code to ask 'How can I help?', analyze the user's answer, and turn a virtual lamp sprite green if the classified intent is 'lamp_on'.
questions.task_hint: ask 'How can I help?' and wait -> if get classified intent of (answer) == 'lamp_on' then set Lamp.Color to Green
questions.explanation: Perfect! This forms a highly responsive, conversational smart home NLP assistant!
